abstract.p: An intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) (10) having improved automated electrocardiogram (ECG) based intra-aortic balloon deflation timing. Said IABP (10) capable of automatically determining to either deflate the intra-aortic balloon upon the detection of the next cardiac cycle (non-predictive deflation) or at an earlier point derived from predicting the occurrence of the next cycle (predictive deflation). This automated determination is based upon a quantitative assessment of the performance of the intra-aortic balloon pump (10) in predicting the prevailing cardiac rhythm. The accuracy of deflation based upon beat-to-beat interval prediction is scored relative to actual beat-to-beat interval. Once the cumulative prediction score of a predetermined number of historic beat-to-beat intervals reaches a predetermined threshold for non-predictive deflation, the non-predictive deflation mode is automatically activated. Scoring of beat predictions continues in this mode to signal when to switch back to predictive deflation.

L'invention concerne une pompe à ballonnet intra-aortique (10) comportant un temps de dégonflement amélioré du ballonnet intra-aortique basé un électrocardiogramme automatisé. Cette pompe à ballonnet intra-aortique (10) est capable de déterminer automatiquement un dégonflement du ballonnet intra-aortique sur détection du prochain cycle cardiaque (dégonflement non prédictif) ou à un point antérieur dérivé de la prédiction de l'occurrence du prochain cycle cardiaque (dégonflement prédictif). Cette détermination automatisée se base sur une évaluation quantitative de la performance de la pompe à ballonnet intra-aortique (10) pour prédire le rythme cardiaque courant. La précision du dégonflement basée sur la prédiction de l'intervalle entre les battements est notée par rapport à l'intervalle réel entre les battements. Une fois que la notation de prédiction cumulative d'un nombre prédéterminé d'intervalles historiques entre les battements atteint un seul prédéterminé pour le dégonflement non prédictif, le mode de dégonflement non prédictif est automatiquement activé. La notation des prédictions de rythme continue dans ce mode de façon à indiquer le moment où il faut repasser au dégonflement prédictif.

description.p: INTRA-AORTIC BALLOON APPARATUS
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION
1. Field of the Invention

The invention relates to an intra-aortic balloon pump navmg improved automated electrocardiogram (ECG) based mtra- aortic balloon deflation timing. More particularly, the invention relates to an intra-aortic balloon pump capable of casing the decision of automatically activating and deactivating non-predictive deflation upon a quantitative assessment of the predictive performance of the intra-aortic balloon pump for the prevailing cardiac rhythm. 2. Description of the Prior Art

It is well-known m the art, as described m, for example, the specification of U.S. Pat. No. 4,362,150, to provide cardiac assistance by introducing a balloon into the thoracic aorta of a patient and causing the balloon to inflate and deflate m anti-phase with the contraction of the patient's heart. A balloon of this type is inflated at the beginning of diastole, m order to increase the blood flow to the coronary and carotid arteries. The balloon is then deflated just prior to the start of systole, m order to reduce the load on the left ventricle. It is essential that cardiac activity be sensed reliably to ensure that the balloon is inflated and deflated accurately with respect to the cardiac cycle .

Methods of sensing cardiac activity include analysis of aortic pressure and/or analysis of the electrocardiogram. It
is known m the art, as described m U.S. Patent No.

5,169,379, to combine means for effecting such analysis with the aforementioned mtra-aortic balloon (IAB) apparatus. The focus of the present invention is the automatic control of deflation timing of the mtra-aortic balloon. Using the ECG as a time-base, a maximum reduction m end diastolic pressure is achieved when IAB deflation begins m advance of the start of the next cardiac cycle, i.e. R-wave. This deflation modality will hereinafter be referred to as "predictive" deflation since the start of the next cardiac cycle must be predicted, based on prior beat intervals. The goal of predictive deflation is to predict the start of the next cardiac cycle and to completely deflate the balloon m advance of the next predicted beat. Algorithms for predicting the start of the next cardiac cycle for a regular cardiac rhythm are generally known in the art of balloon pumping.

One difficulty with using a standard predictive deflation algorithm for control of the mtra-aortic balloon is the potential onset of cardiac rhythm variations. In the presence of random and chronically irregular rhythms, such as atπal fibrillation, accurate prediction of the next ECG beat is not possible. Prediction can be made with only limited statistical probability. Accordingly, such random dysrhythmic patterns are generally managed by having the mtra-aortic balloon pump deflate the mtra-aortic balloon on the leading edge of the R-wave. This method of mtra-aortic balloon deflation will hereinafter be referred to as R-wave deflation. R-wave deflation is a non-predictive deflation method which produces a later deflation of the tra-aortic balloon than that produced by predictive deflation. The advantage of setting the mtra-aortic balloon pump to R-wave deflation mode
m the presence of an irregular rhythm, however, is that deflation of the mtra-aortic balloon begins precisely upon the identification of the next R-wave, regardless of the variance of the rhythm. This enables the mtra-aortic balloon pump to consistently augment the entire diastolic interval and unload the next impending left ventricular contraction.

It is not necessary that all rhythm variations be managed by switching to R-wave deflation. For example, algorithms are known m the art for identifying transient disturbances (dysrhythmia) such as premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) , including isolated PVCs and Couplets, and also for recognizing sudden changes m heart rates. These rhythm variations can be rapidly identified and are typically followed by a predictable beat pattern. Accurate prediction of such beats, after a brief initial learning phase period, is often possible. As indicated above, mtra-aortic balloon pumps presently on the market are automated. The mtra-aortic balloon is controlled by a predictive algorithm situations involving regular rhythms and at least one pump will automatically adopt R-wave deflation upon degradation of the rhythm beyond a threshold level. Bard'S TRANSACT IABP, for example, incorporates an algorithm for determining when to switch to and from R-wave deflation, which is based upon beat-to-beat, i.e. R-R interval, variability.

More specifically, if the Bard mtra-aortic balloon pump detects a large beat-to-beat variation m cardiac interval for 8 out of the last 16 beats intervals then the Bard pump abandons the use of predictive deflation and adopts R-wave deflation control. A major drawback to this method is that the decision to abandon the predictive mode is independent of the success that the mtra-aortic balloon pump is having m
following the timing variations associated with the rhythm disturbance. For example, if a patient's rhythm was such that a premature ventricular contraction occurred on every other beat, and the Bard mtra-aortic balloon pump is designed to successfully track this rhythm, the Bard pump would still abandon the predictive mode because the above described requirements have been met, i.e at least 8 out the past 16 R-R intervals were sufficiently variable to trigger the switch from the predictive deflation mode to the R-wave deflation mode .
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

Accordingly, it is an object of the present invention to produce an mtra-aortic balloon pump which monitors the performance of its predictive mode and automatically switches to a non-predictive deflation mode, such as R-wave deflation, when predictive deflation tracking is compromised by a dysrhythmia, and remains m this deflation modality as long as the cardiac rhythm cannot be accurately predicted. Note that hereinafter any references made to R-wave deflation are also applicable to other non-predictive deflation modalities. An example of a non-predictive deflation mode other than R-wave, is P-wave deflation. In this deflation modality, the IAB is deflated on or after the detected P-wave of the ECG.

The invention is a highly automated mtra-aortic balloon pump capable of basing its decision of automatically activating and deactivating R-wave deflation timing, or another non-predictive deflation, on the predictive performance of the mtra-aortic balloon pump. The accuracy of
each R-wave prediction is scored versus the actual occurrence of the R-wave. Early and late predictions are scored more heavily (penalized) than accurate predictions. Early or late R-wave predictions that occur at the initial onset of a recognizable dysrhythmic heartbeat pattern or rate change, however, are not included m the score. Once a critical score is reached the R-wave deflation mode is automatically activated. Scoring continues R-wave deflation to signal when to switch back to predictive deflation.

To the accomplishment of the above and related objects the invention may be embodied m the form illustrated m the accompanying drawings. Attention is called to the fact, however, that the drawings are illustrative only. Variations are contemplated as being part of the invention, limited only by the scope of the claims.
BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS
In the drawings, like elements are depicted by like reference numerals. The drawings are briefly described as follows.
FIG 1 is a plot of ECG, blood pressure, and balloon state versus time.

FIG 2 is plan view of the mtra-aortic balloon connected to an mtra-aortic balloon pump having a control logic module. FIG 3 is a flow chart illustrating the method of activating and deactivating R-wave deflation m accordance with the present invention.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

Before describing the present invention m detail, reference will be made to FIG 1, which is useful m understanding the principle of the invention. Methods of monitoring cardiac activity for timing of the inflation and deflation of an mtra-aortic balloon include measurement of aortic pressure and measurement based on an electrocardiographic (ECG) signal. FIG 1 illustrates a plot of ECG, blood pressure, and balloon state versus time. The ECG R- wave gives advance notice of the opening of the aortic valve, and the dicrotic notch appears m the aortic pressure at the closure of the aortic valve. Accordingly, the mtra- aortic balloon, following its insertion into the aorta, is adjusted to inflate at the occurrence of the dicrotic notch and deflate relative to the next impending R-wave.

Conventionally, due to the finite amount of time required for deflation, it is necessary to accurately predict when the R- wave will occur and to begin balloon deflation prior to the identification of the next R-wave. Intra-aortic balloon pumps presently on the market are

"automated" to the extent that they are capable of predicting when the next R-wave will occur for rhythmic beats and for some rhythms displaying transient disturbances, such as premature ventricular complexes (PVCs) . In the presence of rhythmic beats the "automated" balloon pump is typically programmed and adjusted to initiate deflation of the balloon prior to the next R-wave so as to allow for complete or near complete balloon deflation prior to the start of systole. In the presence of random and chronically irregular rhythms, such as atrial fibrillation, however, prediction of the next R-wave
is not possible. In such situations the balloon pumps are generally operated to deflate the balloon on the detected leading edge of the R-wave (R-wave deflation) . R-wave deflation results m the heart ejecting blood into a blood vessel containing an only partially deflated balloon. The advantage to R-wave deflation, however, is that deflation begins upon the identification of the next R-wave, regardless of the variance of the rhythm, permitting the pump to consistently augment the entire diastolic interval and unload the impending left ventricular contraction. Reverting to R-wave deflation m the presence of random and chronically irregular rhythms is often preferred. Reversion to R-wave deflation the presence of regular or only transient rhythm disturbances, specifically those recognizable by the balloon pump, however, is unnecessary. The present invention comprises a balloon pump which bases its decision of alternating between a predictive deflation mode and R-wave deflation mode, or an alternate non-predictive mode, as indicated earlier, on the predictive performance of the balloon pump. The basic principle is for the pump to assess and quantify its own performance m predicting the prevailing cardiac rhythm. This is m contrast to Bard'S TRANSACT IABP which bases it decision of alternating between predictive deflation mode and R-wave deflation mode simply on the R-R interval variability. FIG 2 illustrates an mtra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) system 10 having improved automated ECG based IAB deflation timing, comprising an mtra-aortic balloon (IAB) catheter 12, a pneumatic drive module 14, and a control logic module 16. The IAB catheter 12, for insertion into the aorta of a patient (not shown) , is connected to the pneumatic drive module 14.
The pneumatic drive module 14 is m communication with the control logic module 16 via an inflate/deflate line 20. The control logic module 16 has an ECG input line 18 and may also have an inflation and deflation adjustment control line (not shown) . The control logic module 16 uses information communicated via the ECG input line 18, in conjunction with the inflation and deflation adjustment control (not shown) , to determine when to output an inflate signal or a deflate signal to the pneumatic drive module 14 via the inflate/deflate line 20. Upon command from the control logic module 16, the pneumatic drive module 14 inflates or deflates the IAB catheter 12.

The control logic module 16 is programmed to operate the pneumatic drive module 14 predictive deflation mode as long as it is successfully tracking the patient's heart beat. Algorithms for predictive deflation m regular rhythms and also m certain transient rhythms are known m the art of mtra-aortic balloon pumping. The control logic module 16 scores the accuracy of the deflation based upon a R-R interval prediction relating to the actual R-R interval (block 30 m FIG 3) . Note that any beat-to-beat interval other than and including the R-R interval may be used. FIG 3 is a flow chart, each block illustrating one step m the method of activating and deactivating the R-wave deflation mode m accordance with the present invention. In the following example of a scoring methodology, a tolerance window following the predicted R-wave event is such that moderately early predictions are not penalized: A score of 0 for an accurate prediction; A score of 0 for a moderately early prediction; A score of 1 or 2 for a very early prediction resulting m a
very early deflation;
A score of 0 for a moderately late prediction, not resulting an R-wave deflation; and

A score of 1 for a "very late" prediction resulting m an R- wave deflation. The term "very early" is applicable m this example when the prediction results m a deflation so early, it significantly reduces the time available for diastolic augmentation. Significant occurrences of such very early deflates minimize blood flow to the coronary and carotid arteries and compromise unloading on the left ventricle. Notice should be taken that the above scoring arrangement is merely an example and that the "early" and "late" weighting may be varied based upon the clinical significance of the timing variations. The present invention encompasses other such arrangements. Notice should further be taken that an operator has the ability to disable automatic activation of the R-wave deflation mode and assume manual control of the deflation timing mode.

The control logic module 16 keeps track of the cumulative prediction scoring of a predetermined number of historic R-R intervals (block 34 m FIG 3) . If the cumulative prediction score reaches a predetermined threshold for adopting R-wave deflation, the control logic module 16 activates the R-wave deflation mode (block 36 m FIG 3) . Scoring continues m this mode until the cumulative prediction score reaches the predetermined threshold for deactivating R-wave deflation, upon which the control logic module 16 reinitiates predictive deflation (block 38 m FIG 3) . The threshold limits for activating and deactivating R-wave deflation mode may be predetermined values based upon the desired clinical sensitivity.
In this example, if the cumulative prediction score of the past 16 R-R intervals is greater than or equal to 8, the control logic module 16 will switch to R-wave deflation mode, otherwise, it remains m the predictive deflation mode. Further m this example hysteresis is employed, once m the R- wave deflation mode the control logic module 16 will switch back to predictive deflation mode if the score of the last 16 R-R intervals becomes less than 5.

Control logic module 16 is capable of identifying and predicting certain transient rhythm patterns. In the process of identifying a transient rhythm disturbance, one or more initial R-R intervals may not be predictable. This is unavoidable because these R-R intervals occur at the onset of the new pattern, i.e. they are part of the learning phase. Therefore, when the rhythm disturbance is such that it exhibits a pattern identified by control logic module 16, the scoring of the pattern is reevaluated (block 32 m FIG 3) . This reevaluation is performed to ensure that the control logic module 16 does not switch to R-wave deflation mode when it is accurately managing a predictable rhythm disturbance. In the example presented, R-wave predictions scored heavily (1 or 2) during the onset of the pattern are not penalized (reset to 0) if the pattern is successfully identified. Note that the reevaluation technique may be used conjunction with other methods of determining when to switch to and from R-wave deflation mode.

Examples of possible recognizable rhythm disturbances include a premature ventricular contraction (PVC) pattern, characterized by one significantly short R-R interval followed by a longer than normal R-R interval, or a Couplet (PVC pair) pattern, characterized by two successive significantly short
R-R intervals followed by a longer than normal R-R interval, and the onset of a faster or slower heartbeat rate. The term "recognizable" m reference to a PVC, for example, means that upon detection of a premature ventricular contraction the control logic module 16 can accurately predict the occurrence of the next R-wave.

As many apparently widely different embodiments of the present invention can be made without departing from the spirit and scope thereof, it is to be understood that the invention is not limited to the specific embodiments thereof except as defined the appended claims.

claim.claim-text: CLAIMS What is claimed is:
1. An mtra-aortic balloon pump having a setting m which it bases its decision of automatically activating a non- predictive deflation mode on its performance m a predictive deflation mode.
2. The mtra-aortic balloon pump as claimed in claim 1 wherein the non-predictive deflation mode is an R-wave deflation mode.
3. The mtra-aortic balloon pump as claimed m claim 1 wherein the non-predictive deflation mode is a P-wave deflation mode.

4. The mtra-aortic balloon pump as claimed claim 1 wherein the mtra-aortic balloon pump bases its decision of both automatically activating and deactivating the non-predictive deflation mode on the accuracy of beat-to-beat interval predictions .

5. An mtra-aortic balloon pump comprising a balloon inflation and deflation means and a control logic module for controlling said balloon inflation and deflation means, said control logic module having a setting m which it bases its decision of automatically activating a non-predictive deflation mode on its assessment of its performance m a predictive deflation mode .

6. The mtra-aortic balloon pump as claimed claim 5 wherein control logic module assesses the performance of the mtra- aortic balloon pump the predictive mode by scoring the
accuracy of deflation based upon beat-to-beat interval predictions relative to actual beat-to-beat intervals and switches to a non-predictive deflation mode when the score reaches a non-predictive activation threshold.

7. The mtra-aortic balloon pump as claimed m claim 6 wherein the control logic module bases its decision of both automatically activating and deactivating the non-predictive deflation mode on the scoring.

8. The mtra-aortic balloon pump as claimed m claim 6 wherein the score is reevaluated when the mtra-aortic balloon pump is accurately dealing with a predictable dysrhythmic heartbeat pattern or a heartbeat rate change such that scores for beat- to-beat intervals indicating onset of the dysrhythmic pattern or a heartbeat rate change are not penalized.
9. The mtra-aortic balloon pump as claimed m claim 6 wherein the non-predictive deflation mode is an R-wave deflation mode.
10. The mtra-aortic balloon pump as claimed m claim 6 wherein the non-predictive deflation mode is a P-wave deflation mode.

11. An tra-aortic balloon pump comprising a balloon inflation and deflation means and a control logic module for controlling said balloon inflation and deflation means, said control logic module having a setting m which it bases its decision of automatically deactivating a non-predictive deflation mode on a scoring of the accuracy of deflation based upon beat-to-beat interval predictions relative to actual
beat-to-beat intervals and by switching to a predictive deflation mode when the score reaches a non-predictive deactivation threshold.

12. The mtra-aortic balloon pump as claimed m claim 11 wherein the score is reevaluated when the mtra-aortic balloon pump is accurately dealing with a predictable dysrhythmic heartbeat pattern or a heartbeat rate change such that scores for beat-to-beat intervals indicating onset of the dysrhythmic pattern or a heartbeat rate change are not penalized.

13. A method for an mtra-aortic balloon pump for determining when to automatically switch from a predictive deflation mode to a non-predictive deflation mode, comprising the steps of: a) scoring the accuracy of deflations based upon beat-to-beat interval predictions relative to actual beat-to-beat intervals; and b) switching to the non-predictive deflation mode when a predetermined non-predictive activation threshold is reached.

14. The method as claimed claim 13 further comprising the steps of recognizing when the mtra-aortic balloon pump is accurately dealing with a predictable dysrhythmic heartbeat pattern or a heartbeat rate change and m such situations reevaluatmg the scoring of any penalties for those intervals indicating the onset of the dysrhythmic pattern or heartbeat rate change.
15. The method as claimed m claim 13 wherein the non- predictive deflation mode is an R-wave deflation mode.
16. The method as claimed in claim 13 wherein the non- predictive deflation mode is a P-wave deflation mode.

17. A method for an mtra-aortic balloon pump for determining when to automatically switch from a predictive deflation mode to a non-predictive deflation mode and from the non-predictive deflation mode to the predictive deflation mode comprising the steps of : a) scoring the accuracy of deflations based upon beat-to-beat interval predictions relative to actual beat-to-beat intervals ; b) switching to the non-predictive deflation mode when a predetermined non-predictive activation threshold is reached; c) switching to the predictive deflation mode when a predetermined non-predictive deactivation threshold is reached; and d) repeating steps (a) through (c) for each new beat detected.

18. The method as claimed in claim 17 further comprising the steps of recognizing when the intra-aortic balloon pump is accurately dealing with a predictable dysrhythmic heartbeat pattern or a heartbeat rate change and m such situations reevaluatmg the scoring of any penalties for those intervals indicating the onset of the dysrhythmic pattern or heartbeat rate change .

19. An intra-aortic balloon pump comprising a balloon inflation and deflation means and a control logic module for controlling said balloon inflation and deflation means, said control logic module determining when to switch between a predictive deflation mode and a non-predictive deflation mode,
said control logic module not switching to non-predictive deflation mode when it is capable of predicting the heartbeat pattern.
